methodology: Preliminary verse-by-verse comparison of Qur'an 7:126–130 with candidate Hebrew Bible passages. Read published verse translations for Qur'an 7:130 and Exodus 8:19/9:10–11, but did not collate MT/LXX critical editions or manuscript witnesses. Leads are not verified source associations. Checked preceding PR #268 and issues #90, #91, #93, #96–#98. No claim of direct dependence. Existing staged PRs must be reconciled before authoritative counting.

records.topic: Magicians pray for steadfastness and death in submission
records.notes: The Qur'anic prayer follows Pharaoh's threat. Exodus records acknowledgement of divine power but no such prayer; Daniel depicts resistance to royal coercion in a different setting.
records.pending_question: Check pre-Islamic retellings of Pharaoh's magicians; do not conflate Daniel's royal persecution scene with this event.

records.topic: Pharaoh's officials urge suppression of Moses and his people
records.notes: Both narratives depict Egyptian oppression of Israelites; Exodus situates forced labor before Moses' signs, while this Qur'anic exchange follows the magicians' response.
records.pending_question: Collate Exodus sequence and check any pre-Islamic expansion of advisers' speech; distinguish narrative motif from exact speech.

records.topic: Moses counsels Israelites to seek God's help and persevere
records.notes: Exodus has Moses reassure the Israelites at the sea; Qur'an 7:128 offers counsel in an earlier Pharaoh confrontation context and emphasizes the land belonging to God.
records.pending_question: Compare sequence and theological wording against MT/LXX; assess whether Exodus 14 is only a loose narrative motif.

records.topic: Israelites lament oppression before and after Moses' arrival
records.notes: Exodus describes Israelites protesting that Moses' intervention increased their hardship and God's promise of deliverance; Qur'an combines complaint with Moses' prediction of succession and testing.
records.pending_question: Check exact speakers and sequence in Hebrew and Greek; avoid equating promise of inheritance with the identical historical episode.

records.topic: Pharaoh's people afflicted by years of dearth and reduced produce
records.notes: Exodus narrates destructive plagues affecting crops, but does not describe the same multi-year famine in this sequence; Amos' agricultural calamities address Israel rather than Pharaoh.
records.pending_question: Investigate earlier Egyptian famine traditions, separate Joseph's famine from Moses' setting, collate Exodus Hebrew/Greek and date witnesses.
